title: Compiled Python bytecode (.pyc) committed to version control next to the derivation tool
evidence:
diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f807a4d
Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ
--- worktree verification: `git ls-files tools/__pycache__/` -> "tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc"; pyc header flags = 0x00000000 (timestamp-based); `grep -rn "import derive" tools/` -> no matches (script-only, run as `python3 tools/derive_a11y_palettes.py`)
detail: Binary build artifact committed to VCS: unauditable in code review, can silently diverge from the reviewed .py source, and regenerates on every run because .gitignore lacks a __pycache__ rule — inviting further bytecode commits.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc and add `__pycache__/` plus `*.pyc` to .gitignore; the .py file is the derivation record, not its compiled output.
